launch_preconditions: K-1 source/config/token identity unchanged (HEAD==prep, tracked tree clean, config sha256 == launch_plan, token bound to this registration)
GPU distinct from E-0 and DK-1 (ledger also refuses a GPU that already holds a RUNNING worker)
live storage gate: remaining output of the three active runs + >=2 GiB reserve
no OOM / EGL conflict / I-O saturation observed
no additional benchmark attempt (new_rl_attempts_used stays <= cap 3)

measurement.k1_startup_note: K-1 spends its first minutes in the N=0 dev10 evaluation (no transitions); reported separately, not hidden
measurement.ppo_update_wall_time: from 'PPO complete update' log line to checkpoint_generation_published time in persistence/raw_events.jsonl
measurement.sampler: throughput_monitor.py, one sample / 30 s -> throughput/samples.jsonl (per-run transition_log line counts, GPU util+mem, /proc/stat iowait, loadavg, /home free bytes)

mechanism.launch_plan_registered_envelope: launch_plan.json still says workers=2 (registration hash unchanged); this amendment supersedes it for this card only
mechanism.what_was_done: no tracked file, registration file or token was modified; only the K-1 launch wrapper (sha256 recorded in k1_launch_record.json) sets the in-process value to 3 after asserting it is 2, only for plan R-TB-K-1 and only if this file is present with the recorded hash; E-0 and DK-1 processes are untouched and keep their own value
mechanism.where_the_cap_lives: module constant cp_disr.final_tb.MAX_WORKERS = 2, enforced inside Ledger.reserve() (final_tb.py)
mechanism.why_not_a_source_edit: a source edit needs a commit: HEAD would leave prep cac2fa5b3cafb46f1f74370314189f4bca4878fa, which breaks the prep/registration/token identity binding that every train invocation verifies, and the runbook forbids HEAD-changing commits while workers run

operational_thresholds_chosen_by_executo.aggregate_rule: 3-worker aggregate transitions/min over the evaluation window (all-in, same sampler) must be >= the 2-worker aggregate baseline (same sampler, pre-launch window; cross-checked with completed 2-worker update cycles)
operational_thresholds_chosen_by_executo.degrade_rule: an existing worker is 'persistently degraded' if its all-in rate over the second half of the window is < 70% of its own 2-worker baseline AND this is not explained by a PPO/eval phase, or if a PPO update during the window takes > 1.5x its previous update
operational_thresholds_chosen_by_executo.note: the authorization gave no numbers for 'markedly' / 'stable'; these are fixed BEFORE the third worker starts and are reported as my operationalization

stop_rule_as_authorized: if aggregate transitions/min with 3 workers < the stable 2-worker window, or an existing worker's sampling/update keeps degrading markedly: stop the K-1 worker and resume it from its latest complete verifiable checkpoint into a later free slot; never kill E-0/DK-1, never reset their N/T/wall clock
